growth_003:n1.prompt:
You are helping me set up an email marketing account as the first step in configuring our email marketing system (audience, templates, and welcome automation come later). {{vendor}} is our chosen provider for this role.

If you don't already have them, ask me for: (1) my business/brand name, (2) the domain I want associated with this account, (3) the email address I want to use as the account owner/login, and (4) any preferred company details (address, industry) that signup forms typically request.

Once you have these, go to {{vendor}}'s signup page and fill in the account creation form fields: business name, domain, owner email, password field (leave blank or use placeholder text — do not generate or enter a password on my behalf), and any company profile fields requested. Prepare all of this as a pre-filled draft so I can review it quickly.

Do not submit the form, do not verify the email, and do not accept any terms of service or account agreements — creating the account and accepting {{vendor}}'s terms must be done by me personally as the legal account holder, and email verification is something only I can complete. This remains a human step.

When you're done, report back with: a checklist of all the fields you've drafted and their values, a direct link to the {{vendor}} signup page, and a clear note confirming the draft is ready and that you are stopping here — stop for human sign-off before I create the account, verify my email, and accept the terms myself.

growth_003:n2.prompt:
You are helping me set up the audience list for our email marketing platform, {{vendor}}, as part of configuring email marketing (audience, templates, welcome automation). Approval is required before any live changes are applied, so you must prepare everything and then stop for human sign-off.

First, ask me for anything you need that isn't already clear: my domain, a plain-language description of who should be in the audience (e.g., signup source, customer type, behavioral triggers), any custom contact properties or tags I want tracked (name, plan, signup date, etc.), and whether I want the list segmented (e.g., by plan tier, engagement, or acquisition channel).

Once you have this, using my configured credentials for {{vendor}}, draft the following without executing any changes yet:
1. A proposed audience/list structure with the exact name, description, and default fields.
2. Custom contact properties/tags to be created, mapped to my described attributes.
3. Segment definitions (rules-based, so they stay live as data changes) reflecting the audience groups I described.
4. A short explanation of how contacts would be created and updated via {{vendor}}'s contact creation API (in words, not raw endpoint syntax), including how suppression/unsubscribe handling would work.

Present this full draft plan to me clearly, including field names, segment logic, and any assumptions you made. Do not create the list, add fields, or call any API to make live changes — this step requires my explicit approval first. Once I review and approve, stop for human sign-off and wait for my confirmation before proceeding to actual implementation.

growth_003:n3.prompt:
You are helping me create email templates in {{vendor}} as part of setting up email marketing. Before starting, ask me for anything you don't already have: my {{vendor}} account access (confirm you can use my configured credentials), my domain/brand name, links or files for brand assets (logo, colors, fonts), and a brief describing the types of emails I need templates for (e.g., welcome email, newsletter, promotional). If I have existing copy or a rough draft, ask for that too.

Once you have the inputs, do the following inside {{vendor}}: (1) Use the platform's built-in AI drafting/refining tool to propose subject lines and body copy for each requested template based on my brief, so I can review before anything is finalized. (2) Use the visual editor to design on-brand layouts for each template, incorporating my brand assets and personalization tokens (e.g., first name) so they render correctly across major email clients. (3) If I've indicated a preference for code-managed templates, prepare HTML or MJML source with variable placeholders instead, structured so it could be tracked in version control.

Save all templates as drafts only — do not activate, publish, or link them to any live automation or campaign. When done, give me a summary listing each template's name/purpose, a preview or screenshot link if available, and the draft subject line and copy for each. Since a human must explicitly approve before changes are applied, stop for human sign-off once drafts are prepared — do not publish, send, or activate anything without my explicit approval.

growth_003:n4.prompt:
You are helping me set up welcome automation in {{vendor}} as part of our email marketing setup. If you don't already have it, ask me for: (1) my {{vendor}} account access confirmation (use your configured credentials), (2) the audience/list name where new contacts should land, and (3) the welcome email content/sequence I want (number of steps, delays between them, any branching logic).

Once you have these, please:
1. Draft the welcome automation structure: trigger event (e.g., new signup or a custom event fired from our product), the sequence of steps (welcome email, delay, follow-up email(s), any branch/exit conditions), and where contacts enter/exit the flow.
2. Prepare the contact-creation configuration needed to add a person to the audience so they enter the automation (using the add-contact operation), and the event-trigger configuration needed so a custom event fired from our product can start the automation for that specific person (using the send-event operation).
3. Confirm how an ops user could later view an individual's position in the automation and pull/re-enter them without breaking the flow — document this as a note, not an action to execute now.
4. Compile a clear checklist showing: the audience name, trigger event name/payload shape, each email step with subject/delay, and exit rules.

Do NOT create, activate, or publish the automation in {{vendor}} — only prepare drafts, configuration values, and the checklist. Since a human must explicitly approve before changes are applied, you must stop for human sign-off once the checklist and drafts are ready.

Report back with: the full draft automation structure, the prepared contact/event configuration details, the ops-visibility notes, and a plain-language summary of what will happen once I approve.

growth_003:n5.prompt:
You are helping me configure signup forms in {{vendor}} as part of setting up email marketing. If you don't already have them, ask me for: my domain/brand name, the audience/segment description I want to use (e.g., 'newsletter subscribers' or 'trial signups'), any custom fields or tags I want captured (name, company, source, etc.), and where the form will be embedded (website, landing page, etc.).

Using your configured credentials, access {{vendor}}'s account via its documented API or dashboard and:
1. Translate my plain-language audience description into a concrete segment/list definition, including any tags or custom properties needed.
2. Draft the signup form fields, labels, and confirmation/thank-you copy, matching the custom properties above.
3. Prepare the contact intake configuration (how new signups will be created/updated with custom properties) so it's ready to apply at production scale.
4. Read back a summary of exactly who would be included in the resulting segment/list once the form is live, so I can verify targeting is correct.
5. Note any suppression or double opt-in settings relevant to compliance.

Do not create, publish, or activate anything in the live account. Prepare all drafts, field mappings, segment definitions, and configuration values as a clear, reviewable checklist showing exactly what will be created or changed.

Because a human must explicitly approve changes before they are applied, do not submit, publish, or activate the form or segment yourself — stop for human sign-off once everything is prepared.

Report back with: the segment/list definition and expected membership, the drafted form fields and copy, the custom properties/tags to be applied, and a numbered checklist of the exact actions you're ready to execute upon my approval.
